mechanisms.description: In Effects of tranexamic acid on death, vascular occlusive events, and blood transfusion in trauma patients with significant haemorrhage (CRASH-2): a randomised, placebo-controlled trial, baseline ninjurytime may modify treatment response through differential baseline cardiovascular risk.
Patients with different ninjurytime levels may show heterogeneous benefit due to variation in baseline disease burden.
Differences in ninjurytime may alter event risk trajectories, changing absolute treatment benefit.
The association between ninjurytime and outcome may interact with treatment intensity in the trial population.
Variation in ninjurytime may identify subgroups with different competing-risk profiles under treatment.
Trial abstract context suggests ninjurytime could act as an effect modifier for clinical outcomes.
